text:
Noah: Quick one  we're switching 401(k) + FSA vendors on Oct 1. If I'm midyear and already contributed to health FSA and pre-tax 401(k), what actually moves vs what needs manual action? Specifically: 1) will my year-to-date 401(k) deferrals automatically map to the new vendor or is there any break in deferrals between payroll systems? 2) health FSA runout vs carryover  our current plan has a $610 carryover limit; will that carryover still apply after vendor cutover or is it lost? 3) can I change my 401(k) deferral % during the cutover window or is that blocked?

Maya (People Ops): good questions 609 short answers up front: 1) deferrals keep going but we have a payroll blackout for one pay period; 2) carryover preserves value if the plan design stays the same (we're keeping $610 carryover); 3) elective deferral changes are allowed but timing matters. details below.

Maya (People Ops): 1) payroll/recordkeeping: Your pre-tax 401(k) deferrals are taken at payroll and remitted to the plan recordkeeper. On Oct 1 we're moving recordkeepers, but payroll will still deduct per your active election. There is a single payroll run during the cutover week (we call it the "payroll bridge"); deductions will be withheld and the company will transmit to the outgoing recordkeeper and then to the new one as required. There should be no gap in withholding but mapping of YTD balances into the new vendor is a post-payroll reconciliation task.

Jorge - Payroll: adding: the only scenario that causes a short gap is if you submit a deferral change that falls inside the payroll blackout (Oct 2-6). If you want a change to take effect for the Oct 6 pay date, submit it before Oct 1 COB. Otherwise it will process on the following pay period.

Maya (People Ops): 2) Health FSA carryover: carryover is a plan-level design decision not tied to vendor, so since leadership approved the same $610 carryover for plan year 2023->2024, eligible unused funds will carry forward to the new vendor. We coordinate a balance transfer during conversion. However claim runout rules are important: claims incurred in 2023 and submitted by the runout deadline (Jan 31, 2024) will be processed even after conversion, but you should keep receipts until you see your balance at the new portal.

Benefits Bot: Handbook link: https://handbook.redwood/benefits/vendor-cutover-checklist (see sections "Recordkeeper conversion" and "FSA carryover and runout").

Maya (People Ops): 3) Deferral edits: allowed but watch blackout. Also note some vendors treat last-payday-of-month payroll differently for pre-tax percentages vs flat-dollar amounts. If you use flat-dollar contributions per paycheck (rare), confirm with Payroll. For % changes: submit via Workday > Benefits > 401(k) elections. If you hit the blackout, you can still submit a request; it'll queue and execute the next available payroll.

Noah: ah ok. about mapping YTD balances  is there any risk my funds get stuck with the old vendor for >30 days? or will they push through automatically?

Maya (People Ops): reconciliation usually completes within 14-30 business days post-cutover. We run a sweep for stranded balances and have a holdback schedule: a small tension amount is held by the company briefly to reconcile payroll timing differences. If you notice anything weird (e.g., zero balance at new portal but payroll says deferrals occurred), ping payroll with a screenshot and we'll escalate.

Jorge - Payroll: Also: if you recently took a 401(k) loan or in-plan distribution, that can complicate the transfer. If you have an outstanding loan, DM me the loan ID and we'll include loan migration details in the ticket.

Noah: gotcha. last Q   if i enroll in a dependent care FSA midyear (new hire level of enrollment), will that be impacted by vendor cutover? I plan to enroll on 9/20.

Maya (People Ops): dependent care FSA elections are effective with payroll processing rules. If you enroll 9/20 it should take effect on the next standard payroll (likely 9/29). Vendor cutover on Oct 1 won't invalidate enrollments made before the blackout. Just make sure the effective pay date is before the Oct 6 blackout if you want it reflected before cutover.

Noah: thanks 44d i'll submit the deferral change before Oct 1 just to be safe and keep receipts for anything FSA-related. appreciate the help.

Maya (People Ops): perfect. ping this thread if you want us to confirm your PTO/referral/loan state when we run conversion reports.
